target: Tenho de admitir que você tinha razão.
english: I have to admit you were right.
tip: 'Ter de' + infinitive is slightly more formal than 'ter que'.

target: A despeito das críticas, o projeto seguiu em frente.
english: Despite the criticism, the project moved forward.
tip: 'A despeito de' is a formal synonym of 'apesar de'.

target: Acabei dormindo no sofá.
english: I ended up falling asleep on the sofa.
tip: Acabar plus gerund means to end up doing something. Acabei dormindo = I ended up falling asleep, an unplanned outcome.

target: Ela costuma acordar cedo durante a semana.
english: She usually wakes up early during the week.
tip: Portuguese puts the habit in a verb: costuma acordar means 'usually wakes up', literally 'is in the habit of waking'.

target: Porquanto os dados são confiáveis, podemos avançar.
english: Since the data is reliable, we can proceed.
tip: 'Porquanto' is very formal – 'inasmuch as/since'.

target: Contanto que você estude, pode sair à noite.
english: As long as you study, you can go out at night.
tip: 'Contanto que' always takes the subjunctive.

target: Ela deixou de frequentar as aulas.
english: She stopped attending classes.
tip: Deixar de plus infinitive means to stop doing something, as in deixou de frequentar (stopped attending). Not deixar, to let.

target: Ele vive reclamando da vida.
english: He's always complaining about life.
tip: 'Viver' + gerúndio = to always be doing something – habitual.

target: Ele anda se exercitando bastante.
english: He's been exercising a lot.
tip: Andar plus gerund describes something recurring lately: anda se exercitando means has been exercising these days.

target: Ele volta e meia esquece as chaves.
english: He keeps forgetting his keys.
tip: volta e meia is literally 'a turn and a half' and means every so often: volta e meia esquece, 'keeps forgetting'.

target: Ela voltou a praticar natação.
english: She went back to practicing swimming.
tip: Voltar a plus infinitive means to do something again: voltou a praticar means went back to practicing.

target: Acabamos de nos mudar para essa casa.
english: We just moved to this house.
tip: Acabar de plus infinitive means to have just done something: acabamos de nos mudar means we just moved.

target: O professor pediu que fizéssemos silêncio.
english: The teacher asked that we be quiet.
tip: Pedir que takes the subjunctive, not the indicative: pediu que fizessemos silencio, not fizemos.

target: Estou a fim de ir ao cinema.
english: I feel like going to the movies.
tip: Estar a fim de means to be in the mood for or feel like: estou a fim de ir means I feel like going.

target: Você tem que entregar o relatório até sexta.
english: You have to submit the report by Friday.
tip: 'Ter que' + infinitive = to have to. Slightly more informal than 'ter de'.

target: Não é claro que ele saiba a resposta.
english: It's not clear that he knows the answer.
tip: Negating claro que triggers the subjunctive: nao e claro que ele saiba, not sabe.

target: Ela me contou que ia viajar no feriado.
english: She told me she was going to travel on the holiday.
tip: 'Contar que' (to tell/recount that) introduces reported narratives – more personal than 'dizer que'.

target: A gente se fala, falou?
english: We'll talk later, deal?
tip: 'Falou' at the end = 'deal?/okay?' – informal confirmation.

target: Não acho que ele esteja certo.
english: I don't think he's right.
tip: Achar que takes the indicative, but the negative não acho que switches the verb to the subjunctive: esteja, not está.

target: Ela é muito gata, todo mundo concorda.
english: She's really hot, everyone agrees.
tip: gata literally means 'cat'; calling someone gata is Brazilian slang for saying they're hot.

target: Ela perguntou aonde eu estava indo.
english: She asked where I was going.
tip: Aonde, not onde, goes with verbs of motion like ir. Here aonde eu estava indo marks movement toward a place.

target: Que ele faça o que quiser.
english: Let him do whatever he wants.
tip: que plus the subjunctive opens a command: Que ele faça means 'let him do', with no separate word for 'let'.

target: Sempre que eu puder, vou te ajudar.
english: Whenever I can, I'll help you.
tip: Sempre que about a future action takes the future subjunctive puder, from poder, not the present posso.

target: Dado que todos concordam, podemos avançar.
english: Given that everyone agrees, we can move forward.
tip: 'Dado que' + indicative when stating a fact.

target: Há que se reconhecer que houve avanços significativos.
english: One must acknowledge that there were significant advances.
tip: 'Há que se' + infinitive = 'one must' – impersonal.

target: Quer queira, quer não, vai ter que ir.
english: Whether he likes it or not, he'll have to go.
tip: 'Quer... quer' + subjunctive = 'whether... or'.

target: Tenho certeza de que ele vem.
english: I'm sure he's coming.
tip: 'Ter certeza de que' takes the indicative – it expresses certainty.

target: Ficou massa essa comida!
english: This food turned out awesome!
tip: 'Massa' = awesome/great – common in Northeastern Brazilian slang.

target: Eu insisto que ele está errado.
english: I insist that he's wrong.
tip: Insisto que with the indicative (está) asserts a fact you're sure of. Switch to the subjunctive and it becomes a demand that someone act.

target: Eu talvez vou à festa.
english: I might go to the party.
tip: When 'talvez' comes after the subject, the indicative is sometimes used in casual speech.
